On 16 November 1776 its guns returned the salute of the American brig Andrew Doria, the first foreign salute to the flag of the newly independent United States.

forty-years-war.s: The Forty Years' War was a series of campaigns between the Burmese-speaking Ava Kingdom of Upper Burma and the Mon-speaking Hanthawaddy Kingdom of Lower Burma. Ava's kings Swa Saw Ke and Minkhaung I tried repeatedly to conquer the south, while Razadarit of Hanthawaddy held…

france-albert-rene.s: France-Albert René was a Seychellois lawyer and socialist leader who became prime minister at independence in 1976. In June 1977, while President James Mancham was abroad, his supporters seized power in a coup, and René became president.

francesc-macia.s: Francesc Macià was a Spanish army officer turned Catalan nationalist who founded Estat Català and led the Republican Left of Catalonia. On 14 April 1931 he proclaimed a Catalan Republic in Barcelona, then agreed with Madrid to accept autonomy within the Spanish Second Republic.

francesco-ii-ordelaffi.s: Francesco II Ordelaffi was lord of Forlì and Cesena and a leading Ghibelline of Romagna. He defied Cardinal Albornoz's campaign to restore papal rule for years, while his wife Cia degli Ubaldini defended Cesena in 1357 until forced to surrender.

francesco-jacomoni.s: Francesco Jacomoni was an Italian diplomat who served as minister in Tirana before the Italian invasion of 1939 and then as lieutenant-general of the King in Albania until 1943. In that office he held real power over the Albanian Kingdom in personal union with Italy,…

francesco-manfredi.s: Francesco Manfredi was a Guelph noble who became lord of Faenza in Romagna in 1313, founding the Manfredi lordship over the city. He also extended his family's influence to Imola.

francesco-maria-i-della-rovere.s: Francesco Maria I della Rovere was a nephew of Pope Julius II, who arranged his adoption by Guidobaldo da Montefeltro. He inherited the Duchy of Urbino in 1508 and received Pesaro in 1512.

francesco-mario-pagano.s: Francesco Mario Pagano was a Neapolitan jurist and Enlightenment philosopher, author of the Saggi politici. A leader of the Parthenopean Republic of 1799, he drafted its constitution, which drew on French models but added an assembly of ephors to guard it.

francesco-morosini.s: Francesco Morosini was a Venetian admiral who defended Candia during the long Ottoman siege before surrendering it in 1669. In the Morean War he conquered the Peloponnese between 1685 and 1687, and during his campaign in Attica a Venetian shell exploded the Ottoman powder…

francesco-novello-da-carrara.s: Francesco Novello da Carrara was the last Carrara lord of Padua. After Gian Galeazzo Visconti took Padua in 1388, he recovered the city in 1390 and ruled it until 1405, when Venice captured Padua after a long war.

francesco-pico.s: Francesco Pico was the first member of the Pico family to rule Mirandola, north of Modena, named imperial vicar there by the Emperor Henry VII in 1311. A leading Ghibelline of the region, he was also briefly vicar of Modena.

franchino-rusca.s: Franchino Rusca was the head of the Ghibelline Rusca family and lord of Como in the early 14th century, after long struggles with the Guelph Vittani. He also gained control of other towns in the region.

francis-ii-rakoczi.s: Francis II Rákóczi was a Hungarian noble who led the Rákóczi's War of Independence against Habsburg rule from 1703 to 1711. Elected Prince of Transylvania in 1704 and ruling prince of the confederated estates of Hungary, he fought with French support but was defeated.

francisco-de-ibarra.s: Francisco de Ibarra was a Basque explorer funded by his uncle Diego de Ibarra, one of the founders of the silver town of Zacatecas. From 1554 he led expeditions north, founded Durango in 1563 and became the first governor of the province of Nueva Vizcaya.

francisco-de-montejo-the-nephew.s: Francisco de Montejo the Nephew was a Spanish conquistador, nephew of the adelantado Francisco de Montejo, who took part in the final conquest of Yucatán in the 1540s. Leading campaigns into the eastern provinces, he subdued Chikinchel and Ecab and in 1543 founded the first…

francisco-del-rosario-sanchez.s: Francisco del Rosario Sánchez was a Dominican independence leader and member of La Trinitaria, the secret society of Juan Pablo Duarte. On 27 February 1844 he proclaimed independence from Haiti at the Puerta del Conde in Santo Domingo and raised the new flag.

francisco-hernandez-de-cordoba-yucatan-c.s: Francisco Hernández de Córdoba was a Spanish settler of Cuba who led the first European expedition to reach the Yucatán peninsula in 1517. His ships sighted the coastal town of Ecab, which the Spaniards called 'Gran Cairo', and he was badly wounded in fighting with the Maya at…

francisco-hernandez-de-cordoba-founder-o.n: Francisco Hernández de Córdoba (founder of Nicaragua)
francisco-hernandez-de-cordoba-founder-o.s: Francisco Hernández de Córdoba was a Spanish conquistador sent from Panama by Pedrarias Dávila who conquered the lands of the Nicarao and other peoples of Pacific Nicaragua in 1524. He founded the cities of Granada and León.

francisco-pereira-coutinho.s: Francisco Pereira Coutinho was a Portuguese nobleman and veteran of India who received the hereditary Captaincy of the Bay of All Saints from King John III in 1534. His settlement at Bahia struggled and came into conflict with the Tupinambá, who killed him in 1547.

francisco-sabino-vieira.s: Francisco Sabino Vieira was a doctor and journalist in Salvador who led the rising of November 1837 that proclaimed the Bahia Republic, a revolt known after him as the Sabinada. The rebels held Salvador until imperial forces retook it in March 1838 after bloody street fighting.

francisco-serrano-1st-duke-of-la-torre.n: Francisco Serrano, 1st Duke of la Torre
francisco-serrano-1st-duke-of-la-torre.s: Francisco Serrano was a Spanish general and politician who led the Glorious Revolution of September 1868 with Juan Prim and Admiral Topete, driving Isabella II into exile. He served as regent until Amadeo I arrived in 1871, and after the Pavía coup of January 1874 he headed…

francisco-solano-lopez.s: Francisco Solano López succeeded his father Carlos Antonio López as President of Paraguay in 1862. His intervention in Uruguay's civil war led to the War of the Triple Alliance from 1864 to 1870 against Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay, in which Paraguay lost much of its…

franco-hova-war.s: The Franco-Hova War was fought between France and the Merina Kingdom of Madagascar, whose ruling class the French called Hova. French forces bombarded and occupied coastal towns, including Tamatave and Majunga, but could not advance inland.

francois-duvalier.s: François Duvalier, known as Papa Doc, was a Haitian physician elected president in 1957 who declared himself president for life in 1964. He ruled through terror, using the Tonton Macoute militia to kill and intimidate opponents, and drew on Vodou imagery to support his power.

francois-grimaldi.s: François Grimaldi was a Genoese Guelph exile who seized the fortress of Monaco on the night of 8 January 1297, entering disguised as a Franciscan friar with his men. Known as 'il Malizia', the cunning, he held the rock only until 1301, but his family later recovered it.

francois-guizot.s: François Guizot was a French historian and liberal politician who dominated the government of the July Monarchy in the 1840s, first as foreign minister and then as prime minister. As education minister his law of 1833 required every commune to keep a primary school.

francois-martin-governor-of-pondicherry.s: François Martin was an agent of the French East India Company who founded Pondicherry in 1674 on land granted by the governor of the Bijapur Sultanate. He built up the settlement as the Company's chief base in India, lost it to the Dutch in 1693 and resumed control when it was…

francois-tombalbaye.s: François Tombalbaye was a southern Chadian teacher and trade unionist who led Chad to independence on 11 August 1960 and became its first president. He banned opposition parties, and the dominance of southerners in his government fuelled a rebellion in the north and east from…

franco-tahitian-war.s: The Franco-Tahitian War was fought between France and Tahitians loyal to Queen Pōmare IV after Admiral Dupetit-Thouars imposed a French protectorate in 1842 and then deposed the queen. Tahitian fighters resisted from the mountains while the queen took refuge on Raiatea.

franz-joseph-ii-prince-of-liechtenstein.n: Franz Joseph II, Prince of Liechtenstein
franz-joseph-ii-prince-of-liechtenstein.s: Franz Joseph II was Prince of Liechtenstein from 1938 until his death, the first reigning prince to live permanently in the country, at Vaduz Castle. He kept Liechtenstein neutral in the Second World War, and during his long reign it grew from a poor farming state into a…

fraser-river.s: The Fraser River is the longest river in British Columbia, flowing from the Rocky Mountains to the Pacific near Vancouver. The discovery of gold on its lower course in 1858 drew some 30,000 miners, mostly from California, turning Victoria into a boom town and prompting Britain…

frederick-augustus-ii-grand-duke-of-olde.n: Frederick Augustus II, Grand Duke of Oldenburg
frederick-augustus-ii-grand-duke-of-olde.s: Frederick Augustus II was the last Grand Duke of Oldenburg, reigning from 1900 to 1918 over Oldenburg and its exclaves, the Principality of Lübeck and the Principality of Birkenfeld. He promoted the Oldenburg economy, shipping and canals, and was an admiral in the German navy.

frederick-iii-of-nuremberg.s: Frederick III of Nuremberg was a Hohenzollern burgrave of Nuremberg who helped secure the election of Rudolf of Habsburg as King of the Romans in 1273. In return Rudolf confirmed his family's hereditary rights.

frederick-moss.s: Frederick Moss was a New Zealand politician who served as British Resident in the Cook Islands from 1891 to 1898. He persuaded the ariki of Rarotonga and the other islands to form a federal government with a parliament, the Cook Islands Federation, and promoted schools and laws.

frederick-v-of-the-palatinate.s: Frederick V was Elector Palatine and the leading Calvinist prince of the Holy Roman Empire. In 1619 he accepted the crown of Bohemia from the Protestant rebels against the Habsburgs, but his army was crushed at the White Mountain in 1620, earning him the name Winter King.

frederick-v-landgrave-of-hesse-homburg.s: Frederick V was Landgrave of Hesse-Homburg from 1751, ruling the small Hessian state from Bad Homburg. A patron of letters, he was a friend and supporter of the poet Friedrich Hölderlin.

frederick-vi-of-denmark.s: Frederick VI was King of Denmark and Norway from 1808 and regent from 1784, also ruling the duchies of Schleswig and Holstein. As regent he backed the abolition of serfdom in 1788.

frederick-william-constantine-prince-of-.n: Frederick William Constantine, Prince of Hohenzollern-Hechingen
frederick-william-constantine-prince-of-.s: Frederick William Constantine was the last Prince of Hohenzollern-Hechingen, reigning from 1838. A music lover, he kept a court orchestra and hosted Hector Berlioz and Franz Liszt.

free-officers-movement-egypt.s: The Free Officers Movement was a secret group of young Egyptian army officers, led by Gamal Abdel Nasser with General Muhammad Naguib as its figurehead. Embittered by defeat in the 1948 war and by royal corruption, they seized power on 23 July 1952, forced King Farouk to…

free-officers-movement-iraq.s: The Free Officers were a secret network of Iraqi army officers, modelled on the Egyptian movement, led by Abd al-Karim Qasim and Abdul Salam Arif. On 14 July 1958 their troops seized Baghdad, killed King Faisal II and his family and proclaimed a republic.

french-committee-of-national-liberation.s: The French Committee of National Liberation was formed in Algiers in June 1943, uniting Charles de Gaulle's Free French with the forces of General Henri Giraud in North Africa. It acted as the government of France outside German control, directing French forces and the…

friedrich-ebert.s: Friedrich Ebert was a Social Democratic leader who became head of government when the German monarchy fell in November 1918 and, in February 1919, the first President of Germany. He worked with the army to crush the Spartacist uprising and other left-wing risings, and defended…

fructuoso-rivera.s: Fructuoso Rivera was a Uruguayan caudillo and soldier who became the first constitutional president of the Oriental Republic of Uruguay in 1830. A veteran of Artigas's struggles and the war against Brazil, he founded the Colorado party, and his rivalry with Manuel Oribe and…

fu-deng.s: Fu Deng was the last significant emperor of the Former Qin, a Di-led state of northern China. After Fu Jian's defeat at the Fei River in 383 and his death in 385, Fu Deng, a distant relative, took the throne in 386 and fought Later Qin for years in the north-west.

fuad-i-of-egypt.s: Fuad I of Egypt, of the Muhammad Ali dynasty, became Sultan of Egypt under the British protectorate in 1917 and took the title King of Egypt after Britain's declaration of independence in 1922. He clashed repeatedly with the nationalist Wafd party over the 1923 constitution,…

fuad-ii-of-egypt.s: Fuad II of Egypt was the last king of Egypt, proclaimed as an infant in July 1952 when his father Farouk abdicated after the Free Officers' coup. A regency council reigned in his name for less than a year before the monarchy was abolished in June 1953 and Egypt became a republic.

fucine-lake.s: The Fucine Lake was a large lake in the central Apennines of Abruzzo, Italy, around which the Marsi lived. Its uncontrolled floods prompted the emperor Claudius to cut a drainage tunnel in the 1st century CE, though the lake was fully drained only in the 19th century under…

fukushima-masanori.s: Fukushima Masanori was a Japanese warlord who served Toyotomi Hideyoshi and fought for Tokugawa Ieyasu at Sekigahara in 1600. Ieyasu rewarded him with Aki and Bingo provinces, centred on Hiroshima.

fulbert-youlou.s: Fulbert Youlou was a Catholic priest and politician who led Middle Congo to autonomy in 1958 and became the first president of the independent Republic of the Congo in 1960. His government in Brazzaville grew authoritarian and corrupt, and he was forced to resign during the…

fulk-nerra.s: Fulk Nerra, Fulk III, Count of Anjou from 987 to 1040, was one of the most aggressive princes of medieval France. He built a chain of stone castles, including Langeais and Loches, that carried Angevin power into Touraine and against the counts of Blois.

fulwar-skipwith.s: Fulwar Skipwith was an American diplomat and planter who was elected governor of the short-lived Republic of West Florida in 1810. Earlier he had served as US consul in Paris during the negotiation of the Louisiana Purchase.

fundamental-orders-of-connecticut.s: The Fundamental Orders of Connecticut were adopted in January 1639 by the river towns of Hartford, Windsor and Wethersfield. They set out a government of an elected governor, magistrates and a General Court, deriving authority from the freemen rather than from a royal charter.

further-pomerania.s: Further Pomerania is the eastern part of historical Pomerania, lying east of the Oder along the southern Baltic coast, with towns such as Stolp (Słupsk), Köslin and Stargard. It was ruled by branches of the Griffin dukes, passed to Brandenburg-Prussia in 1653 and became part…

fyodor-funtikov.s: Fyodor Funtikov was a Russian railway worker and Socialist Revolutionary who headed the Transcaspian Provisional Government formed at Ashgabat in July 1918 against Soviet rule. His government sought British help from Persia.

fyodor-ivanovich-of-starodub.s: Fyodor Ivanovich of Starodub was prince of Starodub on the Klyazma, a small appanage of the Vladimir-Suzdal lands. Caught up in the rivalries between Russian princes at the Golden Horde, he was put to death at the khan's court in 1330.

fyodor-koriatovich.s: Fyodor Koriatovich was a Lithuanian prince of the Gediminid family who ruled Podolia after his brothers in the late 14th century. He resisted the authority of Grand Duke Vytautas, who drove him out around 1393 and divided Podolia between Lithuania and Poland.

fyodor-the-black.s: Fyodor the Black, Fyodor Rostislavich, was a Rurikid prince of Smolensk who became prince of Yaroslavl by marriage in the 1260s. He spent long periods at the court of the Golden Horde, married a khan's daughter and used Mongol support in Russian princely conflicts.

fabre-geffrard.s: Fabre Geffrard was a Haitian general who overthrew Emperor Faustin I in December 1858 and served as president of Haiti from 1859 to 1867. He restored the republic, signed a concordat with the Vatican in 1860 and encouraged schools and African American immigration.

freikorps.s: The Freikorps were German volunteer paramilitary units formed after the First World War from demobilised soldiers. They crushed left-wing risings in Germany and fought in the Baltic in 1919, where, with the Baltic Landeswehr, they took Riga from the Latvian Soviet government…

frederick-francis-iv-grand-duke-of-meckl.n: Frederick Francis IV, Grand Duke of Mecklenburg-Schwerin
frederick-francis-iv-grand-duke-of-meckl.s: Frederick Francis IV was the last Grand Duke of Mecklenburg-Schwerin, reigning from 1897 to 1918, and from February 1918 also regent of Mecklenburg-Strelitz. His state kept one of the most old-fashioned constitutions in Germany, dominated by the noble estates.

frederick-ii-grand-duke-of-baden.n: Frederick II, Grand Duke of Baden
frederick-ii-grand-duke-of-baden.s: Frederick II was the last Grand Duke of Baden, reigning from 1907 to 1918, the son of Frederick I and a grandson of Emperor William I. During the war he held a nominal army command.

ferdinand-i-of-the-two-sicilies.n: Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies
ferdinand-i-of-the-two-sicilies.s: Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies was a Bourbon king who ruled Naples as Ferdinand IV from 1759. He twice fled to Sicily before French armies, in 1798 when the Parthenopean Republic was proclaimed and in 1806 when Napoleon gave Naples to Joseph Bonaparte.

frederick-augustus-iii-of-saxony.s: Frederick Augustus III was the last King of Saxony, reigning from 1904 to 1918. A popular monarch, he presided over one of Germany's most industrialised states within the German Empire.

fulk-king-of-jerusalem.s: Fulk was Count of Anjou as Fulk V and became King of Jerusalem in 1131 through his marriage to Melisende, heir of Baldwin II. His reign saw a revolt by Hugh II of Jaffa in 1134 and the building of a ring of castles, including Ibelin in 1141, to contain the Fatimid garrison at…

first-french-empire.s: The First French Empire was the state ruled by Napoleon from his coronation as emperor in 1804 until 1814, with a brief return in 1815. At its height around 1811 it annexed the Low Countries, the North Sea coast with Bremen and Hamburg, and much of Italy, and dominated most of…

francisco-alvarez-de-toledo.s: Francisco Álvarez de Toledo was viceroy of Peru from 1569 to 1581 and the chief organiser of Spanish colonial rule in the Andes.
